July 24, 2026

U.S. strikes across Iran as Tehran targets Gulf bases

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual, @hunteralexanderhowell

U.S. missiles struck targets across Iran after President Trump threatened "major military punishment" over attacks on Red Sea shipping. Iran responded by targeting U.S. bases in the Gulf. The exchange comes amid a 13th consecutive day of American airstrikes, with reports that 2,000-pound bombs are now being used.

Pentagon removes four service members from Iran war casualty list

tags: war, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy

The Pentagon removed the names of four service members from its official list of Iran war casualties, saying their deaths occurred after a ceasefire was declared in April. Those removed are First Lieutenant Tyler Feehan, 25, Sergeant Michael Swinton, 30, Sergeant Angel Rampersad, 28, and Private Isabella Gonzalez, 19, who will be posthumously promoted to private first class. Three died in an Iranian strike on a base in Jordan; Swinton was killed by a bomb detonation at an airbase in Erbil, Iraq. The removal was reported on July 23 and confirmed by the New York Times.

U.S. commanders let some Iranian missiles through to conserve interceptors

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Two senior U.S. officials said military commanders are deliberately allowing some Iranian missiles and attack drones to penetrate air defenses in order to preserve a shrinking supply of interceptors. Officials said interceptors are still fired at anything tracking toward U.S. troops, but projectiles bound for areas without personnel may be let through even if they could damage base infrastructure. Iran has fired nearly 9,000 projectiles since the war began.

Selective Service plans computer simulation of national mobilization

tags: defence, government
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

The Selective Service System is planning a computer simulation, called the Readiness Simulation Project, to test scenarios for a national mobilization, according to Military Times. Vendors have been asked to submit simulation models by August 14. Under a proposed rule taking effect in December, men between 18 and 26 would be automatically registered for the Selective Service using data drawn from other federal databases.

Trump says he intends to seek a fourth term

tags: politics, elections
sources: @total.hypocrisy

President Trump said he intends to run for a fourth term as president and indicated an official announcement would follow. The remarks echo comments made in October 2025 by former White House chief strategist Steve Bannon, who said Trump would be president in 2028 and that there were "many different alternatives" to the 22nd Amendment's limits, with a plan to be laid out at an appropriate time.

Hegseth pressed on Iran victory claims while seeking billions more in war funding

tags: war, politics
sources: @ericmoutsos, @total.hypocrisy

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth was questioned in Congress over statements that Iran's military had been "destroyed" and "made combat ineffective" and that the campaign had "achieved every single objective." Hegseth defended the claims, saying Iran's navy, air force and defense industrial base had been eliminated and that the country's capabilities were set back by decades, while declining to say directly whether the earlier statements were accurate. The testimony accompanied a request for tens of billions of dollars in additional funding; the emergency appropriations package is described as $95 billion, including $10 billion for election infrastructure.

Trump reportedly rants in Oval Office over inability to end Iran war quickly

tags: war, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The Wall Street Journal reported an expletive-laced outburst by President Trump in the Oval Office over the war in Iran, driven by frustration that he cannot end the conflict as quickly as he wants. He reportedly called Iranian leaders "scumbags" and "lunatics." White House officials described the president as being in "revenge mode" against Tehran, which they linked in part to 13 straight days of airstrikes.

Republican effort to change election procedures loses ground in Senate

tags: elections, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Provisions of the SAVE Act inserted into the House-passed spending package are expected to fail in the Senate as members leave Washington. The Department of Homeland Security is threatening to withhold public safety grants unless states adopt certain election-related procedures, a move expected to draw court challenges, while the FCC under Brendan Carr is pressuring broadcasters over election coverage. Polling is reported to show rising voter enthusiasm heading into November.

McConnell's whereabouts unknown as Kentucky vacancy deadline nears

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy

Senator Mitch McConnell has reportedly been at George Washington University Hospital for about 40 days and has not been seen publicly in more than 39 days, with no statements from him or his office in weeks. A deadline of approximately August 3 or 4 determines whether an incapacity that becomes publicly known would require Governor Andy Beshear to call a special election; after that date, an appointment becomes more likely. By contrast, South Carolina's constitution required the immediate filling of Lindsey Graham's vacant seat by its Republican governor's appointee.

Ecuadorian prosecutor investigating U.S. maritime war crimes shot dead

tags: legal, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Alexandra Bravo, an Ecuadorian prosecutor investigating U.S. maritime war crimes, was killed in a daylight drive-by shooting outside a cafe in Manta, Ecuador. The gunman was riding a black motorcycle. Her sister was also killed in the attack.

Ukraine expands drone campaign against Russian shipping and warehouses

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Ukrainian drone units report hitting more than 180 vessels and other maritime targets around Crimea over three weeks, claims Reuters could not independently verify. Separately, the retailer Wildberries said Ukrainian drones struck three more warehouses in Russia and Russian-controlled Crimea, with preliminary reports indicating no casualties. Eight of the company's warehouses have been attacked since July 18.

World Food Programme warns of deeper Gaza aid cuts by October

tags: war, health
sources: @oafnation_actual

The World Food Programme warned that further cuts to Gaza aid could begin by October without additional funding. Food rations for 220,000 households have already been halved.

Oil prices spike as questions mount over Kuwait base casualties

tags: markets, war
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Oil prices rose sharply over the week, with claims that efforts to hold prices down artificially are no longer sustainable. Satellite imagery of an airbase in Kuwait was cited as evidence that casualties from a ballistic missile strike may be far higher than officially reported, with estimates of 50 to 100 if personnel were present. The same account said more than a hundred Iranian schoolgirls have been killed and that promised file releases remain withheld.

Trump orders warning signs outside Smithsonian's American History Museum

tags: politics, government
sources: @aaronparnas

President Trump has ordered signs placed outside the Smithsonian National Museum of American History stating that the history presented inside does not accurately reflect American history. According to the New York Times, the order also directs that the signage tell visitors where American history is better presented. The move follows repeated criticism of the Smithsonian by the president.

Fish and Wildlife Service rescinds blanket protections for endangered species

tags: climate, government
sources: @aaronparnas

The Fish and Wildlife Service has rescinded the "blanket rule," instituted in 1975, which broadly prohibited trapping, killing and harassing endangered species. The rollback, first reported by the Washington Post, would apply only to newly declared endangered species; animals with existing designations retain protections. The Interior Department said the change advances directives to strengthen American energy independence and improve regulatory predictability. Species whose designations are still pending, such as the Florida manatee, would be affected.

Resident confronts Casa Grande council over Flock surveillance with satirical proposal

tags: surveillance, privacy
sources: @ericmoutsos

At a Casa Grande city council meeting, a speaker announced a fictitious company, Shepherd Safety, that would use satellites, AI, Bluetooth signals, advertising IDs and commercial data to track the movements of government officials and their families and let authorized users replay them. He said the proposal mirrored the capabilities of the city's existing Flock camera system, including 30-day data retention and restricted access. He then identified the pitch as satire and asked the council to require a warrant for such data, comparing it to phone records.

North Carolina and FDA investigate cyclospora outbreaks

tags: health
sources: @aaronparnas

North Carolina health officials are investigating a parasite outbreak with more than 500 cases since May 1, examining cilantro, parsley and lettuce as possible sources, though no cause has been identified. The FDA said in the past 48 hours that it is investigating a possible new cyclospora outbreak, and it is unclear whether the two are linked. Multiple outbreaks appear to be occurring nationally; doctors noted cyclospora cases are common in summer but not at this level.

Oversight Committee member seeks Barron Trump testimony over Tate brothers

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Representative Yasmin Ansari, a member of the House Oversight Committee, is calling for an investigation into Andrew and Tristan Tate, who face extradition, and specifically into Barron Trump's connection to them. Ansari is asking whether Barron Trump knew of the alleged crimes and whether he or administration officials used their influence to assist the brothers. The New York Times previously reported that Barron Trump had a conversation with Andrew Tate several years ago.

Trump threatens tariffs on Mexico and Canada over lettuce and wildfire smoke

tags: politics, markets
sources: @aaronparnas

In a press gaggle, President Trump said he would impose tariffs on Mexico over lettuce linked to a diarrheal illness outbreak and on Canada over smoke from wildfires. He also called LeBron James a racist, citing the athlete's lack of support for him.

White House social accounts post Iran strike montage set to pop music

tags: politics, media
sources: @total.hypocrisy

The White House's official social media accounts published a montage of strikes in Iran, including footage of destroyed infrastructure, set to Katy Perry's "Firework." The post drew criticism that it made light of civilian casualties and the destruction of hospitals, apartment buildings, bridges and electricity infrastructure. Critics noted such posts pass through multiple levels of approval before publication.

Trump's White House Correspondents' Dinner speech falls flat

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

President Trump's speech at the rescheduled White House Correspondents' Dinner turned into a campaign-style address, with grievances aired against elections, Gavin Newsom and Barack Obama. Attempts at jokes drew silence from most of the room, with the few laughs coming from administration officials including cabinet secretaries and the press secretary.
